body.x: Stereoscopic 3D has traditionally asked viewers to wear glasses or a headset, and it has asked content creators to produce material in 3D from the start. Both requirements limit where 3D displays get used.
What if the same sense of depth came from a display or a phone accessory alone, using video and games that already exist?

MOPIC Co., Ltd., a Samsung Electronics spin-off founded in 2015 and led by CEO Changbong Shin, builds glasses-free 3D technology around that idea. Its business covers Light Field 3D Displays, HoloGlass, a 3D solution for smartphones, and 3D software with SDK and API. HoloGlass won a KES 2026 Innovation Award, and MOPIC is exhibiting it at the show alongside a 32-inch Light Field 3D Display.

The company's core technologies are a proprietary 3D optical lens, real-time eye tracking and 3D rendering. The system tracks the viewer's point of view and delivers a different image to each eye, which produces natural depth and spatial perception. AI-based real-time 2D-to-3D conversion lets existing videos and games be used in 3D without dedicated content production.

HoloGlass consists of an ultra-thin 3D optical lens and a dedicated app, and it converts existing videos, games and photos into 3D in real time using AI. The 32-inch Light Field 3D Display supports real-time eye tracking. MOPIC Hub brings together a 3D Viewer, Player and Capture, 2D-to-3D conversion and device settings in one place. MOPIC also develops and supplies displays in other sizes to match customer requirements.
At the show, MOPIC wants visitors to try the technology firsthand, with the aim of finding new customers and distribution and business partners and widening its industry applications.

MOPIC has worked with a major U.S. corporation for more than 5 years on 3D video-call technology. It supplies microscopy 3D display ODM products to Solectric in Germany, and since 2024 it has supplied HoloGlass and its SDK to a major Japanese telecom company. In Korea, it supplied a 32-inch Light Field 3D Display to the simulation center at Seoul National University Hospital. The company received a CES 2019 Innovation Award and the 2025 NEXTRISE Grand Prize, and it was named to the 2025 FT-Statista Asia-Pacific High-Growth Companies 500.

MOPIC's core overseas markets remain the United States and Japan. In the U.S., it sees potential for the Light Field 3D Display in medical, industrial and content applications. In Japan, it plans to expand HoloGlass through telecom carriers and smartphone accessory retailers. It is also strengthening its SDK and software business to move beyond hardware supply toward integrated 3D solutions, and it is looking for distributors, system integrator companies and telecom partners who can find local customers and provide technical support. Because the difference of glasses-free 3D is hard to convey remotely, MOPIC says, it also wants overseas exhibition and demonstration opportunities.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul, co-located with Smart Biz Expo and the XR & Spatial Computing Show. KES Match business meetings with domestic buyers, global buyers and investors run from Oct. 14 to Oct. 16, and the Innovation Awards ceremony is on Oct. 13.
